title: Gunship
build: original disk, Rapidlok V6, PAL, C64 Preservation Project gunship_s1/s2[microprose_1985](rl6)(pal)

records.c: The 6510's memory layout: $37 the ROMs and the I/O in, $36 BASIC's ROM out, $05 only the I/O in, $00 everything RAM.
The copies' and the unpacker's source pointer, low byte; BASIC puts F here.
The source pointer's high byte.
The destination pointer, low byte; BASIC puts T here.
The destination pointer's high byte.
The copy's length, low byte; BASIC puts L here.
The copy's length, high byte.
The KERNAL's TV flag: 1 on a PAL machine, 0 on NTSC.

Line 0: REM, five DELs and a shifted L ($CC, a byte that is no keyword). LIST prints "0 REM", the five DELs rub it out, and the $CC stops LIST with ?SYNTAX ERROR, so the listing shows nothing but the error.

Line 1: switches off the CIA's timer interrupt (56333), points the NMI vector at an RTI in the KERNAL ($FEC1, so RESTORE does nothing), moves the STOP vector past its test ($F6EA, so RUN/STOP never reads as pressed), and makes the border and the screen blue.
Line 2: clears the screen and prints 129x03 in light blue, near the middle of the blue screen and hard to see: a mark whose meaning is unknown.

Lines 10-11: lowers the top of BASIC to $1700 (23 pages), so the pictures above it are safe from BASIC's strings; MM = 54 ($36, the memory layout for the copies: BASIC's ROM out, the I/O and the KERNAL in); A0-A5 = 165-170, the six bytes $A5-$AA the copies read.

Lines 20-30: loads SMALL, which runs by itself as soon as it is in: Rapidlok returns to its first byte, $8000, and its unpacker turns the packed picture at $97FB into the MicroProse picture at $9800-$BFFF.

Lines 40-60: helpers. 40 splits V into HI and LO; 52-54 put F (from), T (to) and L (length) into $A5-$AA and MM into the A register; 50 copies with SMALL's routine at 32771 ($8003); 60 copies with the library's at 30030 ($754E), once TYPE is in.

Lines 110-140: copies the MicroProse picture from $9800 to $D800-$FFFF with every ROM and the I/O out (MM = 0), and shows it: VIC bank 3, screen colours at $D800, bitmap at $E000, multicolour bitmap mode.

Lines 200-320: loads TITLE, which runs by itself (Rapidlok returns to $8100) and returns here when the tune has played or a key is pressed; then the text screen in the lower-case set, VIC bank 0, light grey border and white screen, and the credits (400) before 470.

Lines 400-460: the credits: design and programming by Andy Hollis and Arnold Hendrick with Sid Meier and Gregg Tavares, screen art by Michael Haire, Michele Mahan and Kim Disney, copyright 1986 MicroProse. Line 460 prints LOAD "begin",8,1 in white on the white screen, where it cannot be seen, for line 512's RETURN to enter.

records.d: 430 PRINT:PRINT"      Sid Meier and Gregg Tavares"
437 PRINT"{blk}Michael Haire, Michele Mahan, Kim Disney";

records.c: Lines 470-480: loads TYPE (the library at $7500) and MAP.CHR.TN, and copies 8000 bytes, a bitmap's worth, from $A000 to $E000 with the library's copy routine.

Lines 500-520: checks the roster (1000), clears the two bytes at 944-945 in the cassette buffer, puts a RETURN in the keyboard buffer and ends with NEW: the RETURN enters the hidden LOAD line, and BASIC loads the front end, BEGIN.

Lines 1000-1020: reads the roster from side 1, track 1 sectors 1 to 4, into $8C00-$8FFF, a sector at a time through drive buffer 1 and the library's read call (KE+69), then calls the check MAP.CHR.TN brought to 28672 ($7000); a zero in $A5 means the roster is good.
Lines 1100-1150: ROSTER DATA HAS BEEN CORRUPTED!, blamed on the drive's alignment or speed; waits for a key, with the CIA's interrupt on just long enough for the keyboard to be read.

records.d: 1110 PRINT"{gry1}  This is usually due to improper disk"
1120 PRINT" alignment or drive speed.  Please have"
1140 PRINT"{blu}      Press a key to CLEAR ROSTER."

records.c: Lines 1200-1220: clears the roster: zeroes $8C00-$8FFF with the library's copy (KE+48) and writes one pilot back, Kilroy: 11 at $8EC0, the name at $8FC0, a 1 at $8FE8.
Lines 1230-1250: writes the four sectors back to track 1 (the library's write call, KE+72, then U2), shows the credits again and checks the roster once more.
Lines 16000-16040: loads the file named in F$ with the KERNAL's LOAD (65493), the address taken from the file (secondary address 1), and tries again until the status shows no error but end of file.
Lines 16050-16080: puts F$ at 830 ($033E) and calls SETLFS (65466: file 0, device 8, secondary address 1) and SETNAM (65469) twice.

The helicopter picture's screen colours, two colours to each 8 by 8 cell, 1000 bytes; the title moves CHOPPER's picture here from $9800 and then copies the first 160 bytes of the logo picture's colours over its top four rows.
The helicopter's screen colours, second page: the colour copy at $8333 reads it into $6100 or $E100.
The helicopter's screen colours, third page, copied into $6200 or $E200.

The helicopter's screen colours from $1AF8: the colour copy's fourth pass takes $1AF8-$1BF7, overlapping the third, so that four passes of 256 cover the 1000 colours and stop short of the sprite pointers at $63F8.
The helicopter's screen colours, rows 23 and 24: where the LDAs at $8C21 and $8C6D point once the helicopter is up, the two rows scroll_colours brings in last.
The 24 bytes after the helicopter's 1000 screen colours: not shown; the last eight are a paint program's sprite pointers, $28-$2F.
The helicopter picture's third colour for each cell (the colour RAM's value), 1000 bytes, which the title scrolls into colour RAM as the helicopter rises.
The helicopter's third colours, row 24: where the LDA at $8CE7 points once the helicopter is up, the last row scroll_cells brings in.
The 24 bytes after the third-colour cells: not shown.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 0 to 2, empty: the rotor frames go above the helicopter's top.
The helicopter picture's row 0, bytes 80 to 159: where copy_row's second LDA ($8B8E) points between copies.
The helicopter picture's row 0, bytes 160 to 239: where copy_row's third LDA ($8B94) points between copies.
The helicopter picture's row 0, bytes 240 to 319: where copy_row's fourth LDA ($8B9A) points between copies.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 3 to 5; the drawing starts in row 5.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 6 to 8.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 9 to 11.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 12 to 14.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 15 to 17.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 18 to 20.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: rows 21 to 23; row 23 is empty.
The helicopter picture's bitmap, 25 rows of 320 bytes: row 24, empty.
The 192 bytes after the helicopter's 8000-byte bitmap: zeros, not shown.

METAL, the title's sprite shapes, 50 of 64 bytes, numbers $C0-$F1 in the VIC's bank 1 ($F000 in bank 3 is a copy). $C0-$C3: the top of the rotor mast, one shape for each of the four rotor frames, sprite 0.
Shapes $C4-$CB: the rotor head, two shapes side by side for each of the four rotor frames, sprites 1 and 2.
Shapes $CC-$D3: the top left quarter of the chin gun's turret, seven views of it as it swivels, sprite 4; $D3 is blank.
Shapes $D4-$DB: the turret's top right quarter, sprite 5; $DB is blank, and the glints use it for none.
Shapes $DC-$E3: the turret's bottom left quarter, sprite 6; $E3 is the shape sprite 1 lays over the letter N.
Shapes $E4-$EB: the turret's bottom right quarter, sprite 7; $EB is the shape sprite 2 lays over the letter S.
Shapes $EC-$F1: two glints, three sizes each, that flash on the turret and on each letter of GUNSHIP as it is drawn.
SMALL's entry, where Rapidlok's load returns: JMP to the unpacker.
The copy BASIC calls (SYS 32771) and TITLE uses: JMP to $80C9.

Unpacks a picture: moves the packed bytes, which end at the address in $97FE, up so that they end at $BFFF, then expands them from $9800 up: a byte is copied, unless it is the escape byte ($97FB), which is followed by a value and a count; the value is written 4 + count times, and a count of 255 is followed by another. Stops when $BFFF has been written, with BASIC's ROM out ($01 = $36) while it works.
The moved data's start becomes the source, $9800 the destination.
Takes the next byte; anything but the escape byte is copied as it is.
A run: the value, written four times, then the count.
The run's count: writes the value that many times more; a count of 255 is followed by another count.
Reads the next packed byte from ($A5) and moves the pointer on.
Writes A at ($A7); when that was $BFFF, drops its caller's return address and returns from the unpacker with the ROMs back in ($01 = $37).
The value of the run being written.
The count of the run being written.
Copies $AA:$A9 bytes from ($A5) to ($A7), upwards, with the memory layout in A put in $01 and interrupts off, then puts the ROMs back ($01 = $37).
Eight bytes between SMALL ($8000-$80F7) and TITLE ($8100): neither load changes them, and nothing reads them.

TITLE's start, where Rapidlok's load returns. Loads CHOPPER and unpacks it, moves it from $9800 to $1800-$3FFF; loads ROTORS and unpacks it to $9800 (the GUNSHIP picture); loads METAL, the sprites, to $7000.

Silences the SID; copies the GUNSHIP picture's top four rows of colours over the helicopter's ($9800 to $1800 and $9C00 to $1C00, 160 bytes each); clears bank 1's bitmap and screen ($4000-$67FF) by copying a zero up through them.

The sprites: all eight on, 0 and 3 hi-res and the others multicolour, sprite 0 twice as tall and wide, sprites 3-7 behind the picture; then copies bank 1 to bank 3 ($4000 bytes, every ROM and the I/O out) so that both buffers start blank.
The tune's tempo for each voice from the TV system ($02A6: 1 for PAL): 2 frames to a length unit on PAL (40 ms at 50 frames a second) and 3 on NTSC (50 ms at 60).
Starts the raster interrupt, a red border and background, multicolour bitmap mode with the bitmap at $4000 and the screen at $6000, and fades the volume up from 0 to 15, one step every 8 interrupts.

The helicopter rises, one pixel line a frame: checks for a key, raises the rotor sound's pitch every fourth frame, and moves on to the next stage once the helicopter is at row 4. At rows 6 and 5 frames without a step come in between, more and more of them, so the helicopter slows and settles.

One pixel up: the fine scroll ($8FBC) counts down from 7, and when it wraps the helicopter's row ($8F88) goes up one; the rotor frame is drawn, and the turret's four sprites are moved up with the helicopter.

What the frame adds to the hidden buffer, by the fine scroll: at 7 it shows it (8520) and scrolls the colour RAM (8C77); at 1 to 5 it copies 4 of the helicopter's character rows (its picture's rows 4-7, 8-11 ... 20-23) a row higher than in the buffer shown; at 0 it scrolls the buffer's screen colours (8BA8).
Asks the interrupt for a new frame ($8F62) and waits until it has been shown.
The helicopter is up: the sprites 0-3 take their places on its rotor, and the hover loop starts.

One frame of the hover: checks for a key, draws the rotor frame, counts the frames ($8FB4). In the first frames the other buffer catches up: the screen colours, then the picture's rows 4 to 23, 4 rows every 8 frames, so both buffers hold the helicopter at its last place.
Copies the helicopter's screen colours ($1800-$1BFF) into the buffer being drawn, at $6000 or $E000.
Copies the next 4 of the helicopter's character rows into the buffer being drawn.

The stages after the helicopter is up: wait for frame 130, swivel the turret (one view every 6 frames) until its frame is below 0, then draw the letters of GUNSHIP one at a time, each with a note and a glint.
Draws a letter of GUNSHIP (8743) into one buffer, then, 10 frames on, into the other and moves to the next letter; after the seventh it silences the third voice and the stage ends.
Moves the glints on: sprite 0's on the letter just drawn ($88B1 shapes), sprite 3's on the turret ($88AD shapes); at step 6 of each letter's wait the turret turns one view back.
From frame 128 of the hover on, shows the buffer just drawn (8520) each frame; then waits for the interrupt.
The letters are done: waits 20 frames, starts the tune (8E78), and loops on the rotor animation until the tune has ended or a key is pressed; then waits 20 frames more and ends the title.
Flips the buffers (8520) and waits for the interrupt to show the frame.
Waits 20 frames, the rotor turning, unless a key is pressed.
The frames title_pause has left to wait.
Reads the whole keyboard: drives all the rows of CIA 1 low and, if any column reads low, ends the title (84AA).

Ends the title: drops the return address, puts the KERNAL and the I/O back ($01 = $37), stops the VIC's interrupt, silences the SID, and returns to whoever called title_main: BASIC's SYS, which goes on to line 300.

Called by the interrupt: copies the sprites' x, y, colour and shape for the next frame ($8F63-$8F82) and the x high bits ($8F83) to the copies it reads ($96C7-$96E7), and the rotor frame to $8FA8; then sets the turret's sprites (88C0).

From the helicopter's height (row times 8 plus the fine scroll) sets the lines of the interrupt's second and third parts (the LDAs at $8A63 and $8A7C) and the y of the rotor's sprites (at $8A22, $8A27 and $8A2C), so all of them rise with it; past line 255 they stay.
Swaps the buffers: $8F8C says which is being drawn (0 for bank 3 at $C000, 1 for bank 1 at $4000), and $8F8D gets the other's page.
The tune's tempo: 3 frames to a length unit for NTSC (index 0), 2 for PAL (index 1).

Draws the next rotor frame (of 4, counted down in $8F89) into one buffer, the other each time ($8F8B), two character rows from the helicopter's row less 2: eight 80-byte copies, their addresses written into the instructions at $868A-$86B7 first. Rows off the bottom of the screen go to $6464, out of sight.
The source addresses for the rotor copy, the frame's strip at $A000, $A280, $A500 or $A780 ($8712, $8716).
The copy: X from 79 to 0, eight LDA/STA pairs 80 bytes apart.
The rotor copy's LDA number 1 ($868A), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 0, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 1, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 1 ($868D), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 0.
The rotor copy's STA number 1, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 2 ($8690), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 80, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 2, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 2 ($8693), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 80.
The rotor copy's STA number 2, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 3 ($8696), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 160, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 3, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 3 ($8699), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 160.
The rotor copy's STA number 3, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 4 ($869C), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 240, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 4, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 4 ($869F), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 240.
The rotor copy's STA number 4, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 5 ($86A2), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 320, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 5, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 5 ($86A5), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 320.
The rotor copy's STA number 5, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 6 ($86A8), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 400, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 6, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 6 ($86AB), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 400.
The rotor copy's STA number 6, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 7 ($86AE), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 480, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 7, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 7 ($86B1), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 480.
The rotor copy's STA number 7, high byte of its destination.
The rotor copy's LDA number 8 ($86B4), low byte of its source: the frame's strip plus 560, set by rotor_frame.
The rotor copy's LDA number 8, high byte of its source.
The rotor copy's STA number 8 ($86B7), low byte of its destination: the helicopter's row less 2 in the buffer, plus 560.
The rotor copy's STA number 8, high byte of its destination.
Clears the character row under the rotor strip (86EF) once the fine scroll is at 6 or 7, so the old frame's bottom row does not stay behind.
Clears 320 bytes, one character row of the bitmap, from the address in the STA at $8703 (and, 256 on, the STA at $870B).
clear_row's first STA ($8703), low byte of the row it clears: the row under the rotor strip, or $6000.
clear_row's first STA, high byte of the row it clears.
clear_row's second STA ($870B), low byte: the row's address plus 255, so with X from 64 to 1 it clears the row's last 64 bytes.
clear_row's second STA, high byte.
Low bytes of the four rotor frames' places in the GUNSHIP picture: $00, $80, $00, $80.
Pages of the four rotor frames, added to $A0: $A000, $A280, $A500 and $A780.
A pause of 2048 reads of $FFFF,X, about 10 milliseconds.
Silences the SID's third voice.

Draws letter $8FB7 of GUNSHIP, five character rows tall, from the GUNSHIP picture ($AA00 on) into row 19 of the buffer being drawn, with the KERNAL, BASIC and the I/O out: the cells at its left and right edges are merged through masks, so the helicopter's pixels beside the letter stay. Then sets the letter's glint and plays its note.
draw_letter's LDA at $877C: the low byte of the letter's place in its row, to which the buffer's row 19 is added for the destination.
draw_letter's LDA at $8787: the letter's carry into the high byte (1 for P), to which the buffer's row 19 is added.
One character row of the letter: the left cell through its mask, the middle cells copied, the right cell through its mask; then the next row, 320 bytes on.
The AND at $8799: the mask for the letter's left cells, from $887C; a set bit takes the letter's pixel, a clear one keeps the screen's.
The LDX at $87A4: how many bytes of the letter's middle cells to copy straight, from $8898.
The AND at $87B6: the mask for the letter's right cells, from $8883.

The letter is in: puts the glint (sprite 0) on it, plays its note on all three voices (885F), and sets sprite 0's high x bit for P, the last. For U, N and H it changes a few cells' colours in both screens ($632C-$637C and $E32C-$E37C); for N and S it gives sprites 1 and 2 the shapes they lay over those letters ($E3, $EB).
Plays a short burst of noise on the voice at offset X: frequency $0300, attack 0, decay 10, sustain and release 0.
For each of the seven letters, the mask for its left column of cells: the bits of the letter's own pixels.
For each letter, the mask for its right column of cells.
For each letter, the low byte of its first cell in the bitmap.
For each letter, the carry into the high byte: 1 for the last letter, P, past the 256th byte of its row.
For each letter, the number of bytes (8 to a cell) of its middle cells.
The shapes of sprite 3's glint on the turret, used from the end: $EC, $ED, $EE, then blank ($DB).
The shapes of sprite 0's glint on a letter, used from the end: $EF, $F0, $F1, then blank ($DB).
The low byte of row 19 of each buffer's bitmap, where the letters go: $C0.
The high byte of row 19, less the 1 the addition carries: $D7 for bank 3 ($D7C0) and $57 for bank 1 ($57C0).
The NMI handler while the KERNAL is out: puts the KERNAL back ($01 = $37) and jumps through its NMI vector.

Sets sprites 3 to 7 for the turret's view $8FA1 (0 to 6; nothing when negative): sprite 3's x from $8F93, shapes $CC+view for sprite 4 and 8 more for each of 5, 6 and 7; and the four quarters' y from the helicopter's row and fine scroll.

Starts the title's raster interrupt: CIA 1's timer off; the RAM vectors at $FFFA-$FFFF pointed at nmi ($88B9) and irq ($8940), the reset too; the raster compare at line 0; $01 = $05, the KERNAL and BASIC out and the I/O in.

The raster interrupt, in three parts down the screen. Line 0: if the main loop has a frame ready ($8F62), sets the fine scroll, takes the new buffer and the sprites' copies, and sets sprites 3-7 (the turret and its glint); shows the rotor's buffer; puts sprites 0-2 on the rotor head; plays the rotor sound and the tune; the next part at the line in the LDA at $8A63.
The LDA at $8A22: the rotor mast sprite's y in the top part, the helicopter's height plus 18, so it rises with it (set by rotor_band).
The LDA at $8A27: the y of the rotor head's left sprite, 29 lines under the mast's.
The LDA at $8A2C: the y of the rotor head's right sprite.
The LDA at $8A63: the line of the interrupt's second part, under the rotor's band: the helicopter's height (row times 8 plus the fine scroll) plus 54.

The second part, below the rotor's band: shows the helicopter's buffer (CIA 2's port A), the next part at the line in the LDA at $8A7C. The third part, from $8A84: sprites 0-2 become the letter's glint and the two shapes over N and S, at the places in the copies; the next interrupt at line 0.
The LDA at $8A7C: the line of the interrupt's third part, 88 lines below the second.
The next interrupt at line 0; then, where the other parts join ($8AEE), acknowledges the VIC and puts back $01, kept in the LDA at $8AF3, and the registers.
The LDA at $8AF3: $01 as the interrupt found it, put back as it leaves.
Copies one character row of the helicopter's bitmap, 320 bytes, from row X of $2000 to row Y of the hidden buffer, the addresses written into the four LDA/STA pairs at $8B88 first.
copy_row's first LDA ($8B88), low byte of its source: the helicopter picture's row, plus 0.
copy_row's first LDA, high byte of its source.
copy_row's first STA ($8B8B), low byte of its destination: the buffer's row, plus 0.
copy_row's first STA, high byte of its destination.
copy_row's second LDA ($8B8E), low byte of its source: the helicopter picture's row, plus 80.
copy_row's second LDA, high byte of its source.
copy_row's second STA ($8B91), low byte of its destination: the buffer's row, plus 80.
copy_row's second STA, high byte of its destination.
copy_row's third LDA ($8B94), low byte of its source: the helicopter picture's row, plus 160.
copy_row's third LDA, high byte of its source.
copy_row's third STA ($8B97), low byte of its destination: the buffer's row, plus 160.
copy_row's third STA, high byte of its destination.
copy_row's fourth LDA ($8B9A), low byte of its source: the helicopter picture's row, plus 240.
copy_row's fourth LDA, high byte of its source.
copy_row's fourth STA ($8B9D), low byte of its destination: the buffer's row, plus 240.
copy_row's fourth STA, high byte of its destination.

Scrolls the screen colours of the buffer being drawn ($6028-$63E7, or $E028 in bank 3) up two rows, since it was last shown two rows lower, and brings two rows of the helicopter's colours in at the bottom, from $1800 on.
The LDA at $8C21, low byte: where scroll_colours takes the two new rows of colours for bank 1's screen.
The LDA at $8C21, high byte.
The LDA at $8C6D, low byte: where scroll_colours takes the two new rows for bank 3's screen.
The LDA at $8C6D, high byte.
Waits for line $30, marks the frame ready ($8F62), and scrolls the colour RAM up one row, 24 rows of 40, bringing the helicopter's next row of third colours in at the bottom from $1C00 on.
The LDA at $8CBD, low byte: the colour RAM row scroll_cells moves up, starting at row 1 ($D828).
The LDA at $8CBD, high byte.
The STA at $8CC0, low byte: the colour RAM row it goes to, starting at row 0 ($D800).
The STA at $8CC0, high byte.
The LDA at $8CE7, low byte: the helicopter's row of third colours that enters colour RAM's last row.
The LDA at $8CE7, high byte.
Loads file A of three, CHOPPER, ROTORS or METAL, from drive 8 to its address in the tables at $8D21-$8D41, through SETLFS, SETNAM and the KERNAL's LOAD.
The three file names: CHOPPER, ROTORS, METAL.
Low bytes of the three names' addresses.
High bytes of the names' addresses.
The names' lengths: 7, 6, 5.
Low bytes of the load addresses: $97FB, $97FB, $7000.
High bytes of the load addresses.
Low bytes of each character row's offset in a bitmap, row times 320, rows 0 to 24.
High bytes of the rows' offsets in a bitmap.
Low bytes of each row's offset in a screen, row times 40, rows 0 to 24.
High bytes of the rows' offsets in a screen.

The rotor's sound, once a frame: each voice switches its gate on and off with its own timing; at each switch its pitch goes back to its start, and each frame between a step is added to it. Once the first letter is drawn ($8FB8) it only counts the frame ($96F0).
The LDX at $8DCF: the last voice the rotor sound works on, 2, so all three.
Writes the voice's pitch to the SID, high byte then low; then the next voice down, and the frame is counted ($96F0).
0 until the rotor sound has set the SID up from $8E63.
For each voice, how long its gate stays on: 4, 3 and 2, each a frame less than it lasts.
For each voice, how long its gate stays off: 0, a single frame.
For each voice, its control register, the gate bit toggled: noise, noise and pulse.
The second voice's control register, gate bit toggled: noise.
The third voice's control register, gate bit toggled: pulse.
For each voice, the low byte of its pitch at the start of each beat.
For each voice, the high byte of its pitch at the start of each beat; the third (at $8E59) goes up every fourth frame while the helicopter rises, so the whine climbs.
The third voice's pitch at each beat, high byte, raised every fourth frame while the helicopter rises.
For each voice, the step added to its pitch each frame: $7F, -12, $7F.
Each voice's first register in the SID: 0, 7, 14.
For each voice, the frames left until its gate changes.
The SID's first 21 registers for the rotor sound: the three voices' frequencies, pulse widths, waveforms and envelopes.
Starts the tune: sets the SID's 25 registers from $90FE and marks it playing ($8F52 = 0).

Plays the tune, once a frame: for each voice whose note has run out, the gate goes off, the next note is read from its stream and its frequency set from the tables at $9006 and $9082, and the next byte, the length, times the tempo, is how many frames it lasts; a note of $80 is a rest and $81 ends the tune.
The next voice down, 2 to 0.
Reads the next byte of the voice's stream, from the address written into its LDA, and moves on.
The LDA at $8F18, low byte: where the voice's stream is read next.
The LDA at $8F18, high byte.
Multiplies A by Y, 8 bits by 8, the product kept in the LDA at $8F48 and returned in A.
The LDA at $8F48: the product multiply builds and returns.
The voice the tune player is on, 2 down to 0.
The note just read: below $80 a note, $80 a rest, $81 the end.
The multiplier, shifted left each step.
The multiplicand, shifted right each step.
For each voice, non-zero if it plays: all three are $09.
